profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, who had previously built companies acquired by IXC Communications. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company opened what it described as the largest data center in Texas in Carrollton in 2012, the anchor of the Dallas Fort Worth cluster that this registry row is part of, alongside CyrusOne buildings in nearby Allen, Lewisville, and Collin County. CyrusOne also operates a substantial San Antonio campus and an Austin facility, both long-running Texas markets for the company, though no specific acquisition or opening story for San Antonio or Austin individually was located in available sourcing this session. The company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for 525 million dollars in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne SAT1 publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 110,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at a more modest 10 kW per rack, typical of mixed enterprise colocation, the same power budget reaches around 900 racks. Those are assumptions about density, not operator claims. The campus sits at the lower end of what operators publish: it ranks eighth out of eight Texas facilities for which this site has read a megawatt figure, against a published state total of 315 MW across those eight sites, meaning SAT1 represents roughly 2.9 percent of that published total. Texas has 133 mapped facilities in total, and most publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is larger by an unknown amount.

The certifications tell a specific story about workload eligibility. PCI DSS qualifies the campus to host payment card processing environments. HIPAA qualifies it for regulated healthcare data. ISO 27001 certifies an information security management system against an international standard. FISMA qualifies it for certain federal government workloads. SSAE 16 Type II documents that controls were tested over a period of time, not merely described at a point in time. TIA-942 is a design standard for data center infrastructure. Together, the certifications position SAT1 for compliance-sensitive tenants in finance, healthcare, and government rather than for hyperscale AI training, which generally prioritizes raw power density over audit frameworks.

For a reader evaluating AI relevance, 9 MW is a meaningful threshold. It is enough to run a serious inference workload or a mid-size fine-tuning cluster, but it is not the scale at which frontier model training occurs, which typically requires dedicated campuses in the hundreds of megawatts. The compliance certifications add value for regulated AI deployments, such as healthcare inference pipelines or federal agency models, where audit requirements constrain where compute can sit. Whether CyrusOne has expanded capacity beyond the published 9 MW figure, or has announced plans to do so, is not published on the spec page this site read.
